punchline: A UPS employee who never earned more than about $14,000 a year built a fortune of around $70 million.
thirty_sec: In Money: Master the Game, Tony Robbins tells of Theodore Johnson, an early UPS worker who never earned more than about $14,000 a year. His rule: save 20 percent of every paycheck and bonus, largely in company stock. By age 90, he had around $70 million. Robbins's lesson is compounding: consistency and time matter more than income, though Johnson also benefited from UPS stock doing extremely well.
question: What fixed rule could you set for your savings starting this month?
